plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in delicate, silky blooms with golden stamens. They brighten gardens and hedgerows just as most other plants are fading for winter, and they give a light, tea-like perfume.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter, usually October or November through December or January
plants.location: Southern Japan, and gardens in the southeastern United States and mild temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: Sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant (Camellia sinensis). Its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, which has long been used in Japan for cooking and hair care.

plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: This jungle cactus has chains of flat, scalloped green stems. Each stem tip carries a bright, asymmetrical flower with swept-back petals. In the wild it clings to tree branches and rocks in misty mountain forests.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-November through late December, sometimes into January
plants.location: Atlantic Forest mountains of southeastern Brazil, and indoors worldwide
plants.funFact: Unlike desert cacti, it grows on trees as an epiphyte. Its tubular flowers are pollinated by hummingbirds in the wild.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: In its native habitat this is a tall, leggy shrub topped with fiery rosettes. The flaming colors come from modified leaves called bracts. The true flowers are the tiny golden-yellow cups in the center.
plants.location: Southern Mexico, where it grows wild, and warm gardens and homes worldwide
plants.funFact: The bracts turn color in response to the long nights of late autumn. The Aztecs called the plant cuetlaxochitl and used its sap and bracts for medicine and dye.
